# Supported formats

The core knows **615** formats: **515** can be read (decoded) and **424** can be written (encoded).

- **Read**: the core has a reader for the format, so it can be the source of a conversion.
- **Write**: the core has a writer, so it can be a conversion target.
- A format with neither is still *detected* (the apps name it correctly), and any file,
  readable or not, can be turned into the universal byte targets of the encodings
  category (Base64, hexadecimal, checksums and similar).
- Same-format conversion (for example PNG to PNG at a lower quality) is offered as
  "Compress" wherever a format can be both read and written.

What can be converted into what is decided at run time by the planner; ask the CLI with
`convertible targets <file-or-format>`.

## Encodings and checksums

| ID | Name | Extensions | Read | Write | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | :---: | :---: | --- |
| `a1z26` | A1Z26 cipher | `.a1z26` | yes | yes | Classic puzzle code, not encryption: letters as their positions 1-26 ("hi" -> "8-9"). |
| `ascii85` | Ascii85 text | `.a85`, `.ascii85` | yes | yes | Adobe's Base85 encoding as used in PostScript and PDF: five characters for four bytes. |
| `asm-bytes` | Assembly data listing | `.asm`, `.s`, `.inc` | yes | yes | The bytes as assembler data directives: NASM/MASM `db` or GNU as `.byte`. |
| `atbash` | Atbash cipher | `.atbash` | yes | yes | Classic cipher, not encryption: the alphabet reversed (A<->Z, B<->Y ...). |
| `authorized-keys` | OpenSSH authorized_keys | `.authorized_keys` | yes | yes | Authorised public keys with options. |
| `base122` | Base122 text | `.b122`, `.base122` | yes | yes | Base122: 7 bits per UTF-8 character, a compact way to embed binary data in HTML. |
| `base16` | Base16 text | `.b16`, `.base16` | yes | yes | RFC 4648 Base16: upper-case hexadecimal, two digits per byte. |
| `base32` | Base32 text | `.b32`, `.base32` | yes | yes | Binary data as the letters A-Z and digits 2-7 (RFC 4648). |
| `base32-crockford` | Base32 text (Crockford alphabet) | `.b32crockford`, `.crockford` | yes | yes | Base32 without the easily confused letters I, L, O and U, for codes that people read aloud or type. |
| `base32hex` | Base32 text (extended hex alphabet) | `.b32hex`, `.base32hex` | yes | yes | Base32 with the digits 0-9 and letters A-V, which keeps the sort order of the data (RFC 4648). |
| `base36` | Base36 text | `.b36`, `.base36` | yes | yes | The file as one big number written with the digits 0-9 and letters a-z; for files up to 64 KiB. |
| `base45` | Base45 text | `.b45`, `.base45` | yes | yes | RFC 9285 Base45, the alphanumeric encoding used in QR codes. |
| `base58` | Base58 text | `.b58`, `.base58` | yes | yes | The Bitcoin alphabet: letters and digits without 0, O, I and l; for files up to 64 KiB. |
| `base58check` | Base58Check text | `.b58c`, `.base58check` | yes | yes | Base58 with a 4-byte double SHA-256 checksum, as in Bitcoin addresses and keys. |
| `base62` | Base62 text | `.b62`, `.base62` | yes | yes | The file as one big number written with 0-9, A-Z and a-z; for files up to 64 KiB. |
| `base64` | Base64 text | `.b64`, `.base64` | yes | yes | Binary data as printable ASCII (RFC 4648). |
| `base64-json` | Base64 JSON envelope | `.json`, `.b64.json` | yes | yes | A JSON object with the file name, media type, size, SHA-256 and the content as Base64. |
| `base64-mime` | Base64 text (MIME) | `.b64`, `.mime` | yes | yes | Base64 as in e-mail bodies (RFC 2045): 76 characters per line, CRLF line breaks. |
| `base64url` | Base64 URL-safe text | `.b64url` | yes | yes | Base64 with '-' and '_' so it can be used in URLs and file names. |
| `base91` | basE91 text | `.b91`, `.base91` | yes | yes | basE91: about 23% overhead, using 91 printable ASCII characters. |
| `base92` | Base92 text | `.b92`, `.base92` | yes | yes | Base92: 13 bits in two printable ASCII characters. |
| `bech32` | Bech32 text | `.bech32` | yes | yes | Bech32 or Bech32m (BIP 173/350): a prefix, '1', 5-bit data and a 6-character checksum. |
| `bin` | Raw binary data | `.bin` | - | yes | The bytes of the file, unchanged or decoded from a text encoding. |
| `binary-text` | Binary digits | `.bits` | yes | yes | Every byte as eight 0/1 characters. |
| `blake2b` | BLAKE2b checksum | `.b2` | - | yes | The BLAKE2b digest of the file, as hex, a blake2bsum-style line, Base64 or another notation. |
| `blake2s` | BLAKE2s checksum | `.blake2s` | - | yes | The BLAKE2s digest of the file, as hex, a blake2ssum-style line, Base64 or another notation. |
| `blake3` | BLAKE3 checksum | `.b3` | - | yes | The BLAKE3 digest of the file, as hex, a blake3sum-style line, Base64 or another notation. |
| `braille` | Braille (Grade 1) | `.brl` | yes | yes | Uncontracted English braille written with Unicode braille cells (capital and number signs). |
| `bytes-inc` | Byte list include file | `.inc` | yes | yes | Comma-separated 0x.. values to #include inside a C/C++ array initialiser (or any build tool). |
| `c-header` | C array header | `.h` | - | yes | The file as an unsigned char array for embedding in C or C++. |
| `caesar` | Caesar cipher (ROT-N) | `.caesar` | yes | yes | Classic cipher, not encryption: every letter shifted N places in the alphabet. |
| `charset-detect` | Text encoding report | `.txt`, `.charset` | - | yes | The most likely character encodings of a text file, with a confidence for each. |
| `checksums` | Checksum report | `.txt`, `.checksums` | - | yes | Size and checksums of the file (by default CRC-32, Adler-32, MD5, SHA-1 and SHA-256). |

| `csharp-array` | C# byte array | `.cs` | - | yes | The file as a byte[] initialiser for C#. |
| `data-uri` | Data URI | `.txt`, `.datauri` | yes | yes | The file embedded in a data: URL for use in HTML or CSS. |
| `decimal` | Decimal byte values | `.dec`, `.decimal` | yes | yes | Every byte as a decimal number from 0 to 255. |
| `der` | DER certificate/key | `.der`, `.cer`, `.crt` | yes | yes | Binary ASN.1 DER certificate, request, CRL or key. |
| `go-array` | Go byte slice | `.go` | - | yes | The file as a []byte literal for Go. |

| `hash` | Hash or checksum | `.hash` | - | yes | Any of about 70 hash functions and checksums (SHA-2/3, BLAKE2/3, RIPEMD, CRC, xxHash, ...), with HMAC. |
| `hex` | Hexadecimal text | `.hex` | yes | yes | Two hexadecimal digits per byte. |
| `hexdump` | Hex dump | `.txt`, `.hexdump`, `.xxd` | yes | yes | Offsets, hexadecimal bytes and printable characters, like xxd. |

| `hqx` | BinHex 4.0 | `.hqx` | yes | yes | Classic Mac OS BinHex: CRC-checked, run-length packed 6-bit text. |
| `html-entities` | HTML-escaped text | `.htmlentities` | yes | yes | Text with the characters that are special in HTML written as entities such as &amp;. |
| `idna` | Internationalised domain names | `.idna` | yes | yes | Domain names (one per line) converted to their ASCII xn-- form (UTS #46 basics), and back. |
| `ihex` | Intel HEX | `.hex`, `.ihex`, `.ihx`, `.a43`, `.a90` | yes | yes | Firmware image as Intel HEX records with addresses and checksums. |
| `java-array` | Java byte array | `.java` | - | yes | The file as a byte[] initialiser for Java. |
| `js-array` | JavaScript Uint8Array | `.js` | - | yes | The file as a Uint8Array for JavaScript. |
| `json-string` | JSON string literal | `.jsonstr` | yes | yes | The whole text as one quoted and escaped JSON string. |
| `jwk` | JSON Web Key | `.jwk`, `.jwks` | yes | yes | JWK or JWK Set (public keys). |
| `jwt` | JSON Web Token | `.jwt` | yes | - | Compact JWT/JWS/JWE; decoded without verification. |
